items.original_prompt:
Create a fresh painted anatomical reference of the exact Veilwing in the two original reference paintings. Use those originals for head, leaf-feather covering, hooked wing shape, muted warm ivory/ochre/dusty lavender colours and plain brown leather equipment. Reset to their restrained saturation and oil/acrylic handling. Do not copy unclear original wing attachments. Pale warm-grey paper, soft neutral light, no landscape, no drama. One large view only, not a crowded multi-panel sheet. The anatomy is substantial, graceful and huge: a full gently elongated torso with a short integrated neck, not a skinny snake. Body from snout to rump is SHORTER than one fully extended shoulder wing. Each of the FOUR tail streamers is LONGER than the snout-to-rump body. Short body, enormous matched shoulder wings, very long fine tails are the visual proportion relationships; do not shrink the appendages to fit. Exactly two lateral shoulder wings, two separately rooted back sails, and four tufted tails. Do not add legs or extra fins. The paired shoulder wings share the same transverse root station at the front third of the body. Each is a mirror counterpart with the same broad membrane, scalloped trailing edge and hooked terminal point. Back sail D1 is rooted at mid-back, behind the shoulders; D2 has its own more posterior root before the rump. Both can lean sideways, with free edges not fused to torso. Harness lightly indicated over solid torso only, no strap through a moving root. Every tail is a slender continuous stem from the rump with one small leaflike terminal tuft, and there are EXACTLY FOUR, never five. No bare extra filament.
TRUE ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP VIEW, head at top center, rump below it, four tails trailing downward. The body occupies only about ONE THIRD of the sheet HEIGHT. Its two huge fully spread shoulder wings reach far to the left and right in a matched symmetrical pair, each root-to-hook visibly longer than the body. Both wing roots must sit on the SAME horizontal shoulder line. Show BOTH complete hooks; no cropping. In this view the two vertical dorsal sails are seen EDGE-ON as two distinct narrow root ridges arranged front-to-back along the spine; do not spread them into an extra wing pair. Mark these root locations D1 and D2. Draw the four tails extending much farther below the rump than the body's own length, fanned just enough to distinguish four fine stems and four modest tufts. Four tails labeled T1, T2, T3, T4 at their terminal tufts, no fifth. Keep adequate empty margins; scale the WHOLE creature down uniformly if needed, not the wings or tails. A thin transverse guide joins the opposing shoulder roots, with small dots on the roots; label 'SHARED SHOULDER LINE'. A thin body axis helps distinguish spine, sail bases and rump. Concise outside labels only: 'VA1 • TOP / ROOT MAP', 'LEFT', 'RIGHT', 'D1', 'D2', 'TAIL ROOTS', 'T1', 'T2', 'T3', 'T4'. No numerical ratio chart. The labels must point to correct anatomical sides: in top view with head up, the animal's left is page-left. Painted body and wings, delicate technical leaders, clear readable anatomy.

items.prompt:
Edit this ORIGINAL R2 painting into a corrected creature reference. This exact image is the authority for the long slender character, colours, head, harness, tail texture and quiet painted atmosphere. Do not substitute the short thick drake-like body of the later studies. Preserve the original muted warm ivory, dusty lavender and ochre, soft coherent light and oil/acrylic paint handling. Ancient strength and mystery: a slender, long, immense creature with enormous wings and gently flowing tails.

CORRECT THE CONTINUOUS BODY FIRST. In the original, the slender torso carrying the harness seems to continue right beneath the middle sail, while a different branch below it carries the tails too early. These must be ONE body, not a fork. Follow the beautiful long slender contour of the harness-bearing torso. Extend that single continuous body beneath the big middle/front dorsal sail toward its lower trailing pointed tip, ending just BEFORE that tip, not past it. In the original coordinates, the real rump should end near x900,y490, approaching but staying short of the middle sail's lower point near x970,y530. This is a broad spatial guide, not a contour to trace. Keep the body elegant and slim with an uninterrupted subtle shaded underside; do not make a fat belly or a long thin neck. No second torso hanging below it. The sail stays a distinct mobile membrane above that body with its own free edge and root.

TAILS: remove the premature tail-bearing branch beneath midbody. All FOUR tails now grow naturally from the single true posterior end of the lengthened torso. Preserve what is beautiful in R2: each tail begins with a substantial softly feathered taper, becomes a very long thin supple stem, and opens into a modest leaflike terminal fan. Four complete tails, four fans, no additional bare filaments. They drift in graceful different curves as if in a gentle breeze, not straight wires or identical ribbons. Make them a little longer than R2's tails; their total curving length is at least comparable to the NEW long snout-to-rump body. Never shorten them to fit the page. Pull back the framing uniformly enough to fit every tip with breathing room while preserving the longer body and enormous wing scale.

ADD THE MISSING NEAR LEFT SHOULDER WING. We are viewing the left side. The visible shoulder between the FIRST TWO leather buckles nearest the head is currently bare. A huge LEFT front wing must grow from that gap, from the lateral shoulder beneath the top leather connector. Keep the original existing downstroking RIGHT/front wing on the far side; the creator likes it. The new left wing attaches directly opposite that existing right wing at the SAME shoulder cross-section, not from the middle or rear of the body. It is the same actual anatomical wing type: very large broad leaf-feather membrane, curved leading edge, scalloped trailing edge and long slender hooked terminal point. Let the near left wing descend into the lower foreground, partly overlapping the existing far/right wing naturally, while keeping BOTH hooked tips visibly separated. Preserve the original right wing's shape; do not replace it with a short triangle. Keep the harness clear of the moving root; no strap through the membrane.

Preserve BOTH original dorsal sails, their broad swept shapes and their separate mobile back attachments. This completes exactly FOUR flight surfaces: left front, right front, front dorsal sail, rear dorsal sail. No fifth membrane, neck flap or belly fin. Keep the original face, feelers, plain leather equipment and natural soft colour. Retain the simple original distant ground/sky only as a quiet backdrop, with no huge shadow or new buildings. No annotations, text or labels. This is the single long-bodied anatomical reference from R2, not a compact new species.
